title: Teacher Workflow No. 06: you gave that lecture once, and it's already gone
author: Doan Winkel
summary: Doan Winkel offers a five-step teacher workflow that turns a single phone recording of a lecture into four reusable documents: a study guide, a quiz, a catch-up brief for absent students, and a confusion note for next year. He starts from the familiar pattern of study-guide requests and missed-class emails that arrive after a lecture has been given once and forgotten. The process runs record, scrub, build in NotebookLM, verify, and ship to the LMS, and it takes roughly forty minutes including checking. He insists on removing every student name before anything is uploaded and on using Ctrl-F to confirm it. The verification step is the core of the piece: because NotebookLM footnotes answers back to the transcript, the teacher can click each citation and decide what to trust. A minimal version, recording only the lecture before a midterm, is offered for teachers who want to start small.
points: One unrecorded lecture is a lost asset, and a phone recording becomes the raw material for a study guide, a quiz, a catch-up brief, and a note to next-year-you.
The privacy step comes before any AI step: scrub student names, questions, grades, and accommodations from the transcript, and search every roster first name with Ctrl-F.
Untick every NotebookLM source except the current lecture so that week nine's study guide does not draw on week three.
Verification is concrete: click every citation, answer half the quiz cold yourself, and retype the catch-up brief's next-class line instead of re-running the prompt.
The smallest useful version is to record only the lecture before the midterm and generate just the study guide and catch-up brief.
quotes: You said all of it out loud on Tuesday. The examples, the detour you took when half the room looked lost. Forty students heard it once, and the version that survives is whatever landed in their notes.
Stop the recording before any stretch where students talk at length. A discussion is theirs. Your lecture is yours.
Then search the transcript for every first name on your roster. Ctrl-F, not a read-through. A name you skimmed past is a name you uploaded.
Before you run anything, untick every source in the left panel except today’s. Otherwise week nine’s study guide pulls from week three.
NotebookLM footnotes its answers back to your transcript. The footnotes are the check, and this is where you stop trusting the machine.
Quiz: answer four of the eight yourself, cold, before you read the key. Any key you’d mark wrong on a student’s paper gets rewritten by you.
Don’t record every class. Record the next one, the lecture right before the midterm, and run the study guide and the catch-up brief only.
Skip it, and you’ll rebuild the study guide from the slides at 10pm Wednesday, then explain Tuesday’s lecture again in office hours, one student at a time.
